Telugu Festivals 2035 / తెలుగు పండుగలు 2035

तेलुगु पंचांग दक्षिणी अमान्त चन्द्र-सौर कैलेंडर पर आधारित है, जिसमें महीना अमावस्या से अमावस्या तक चलता है। इसका उपयोग आंध्र प्रदेश, तेलंगाना, कर्नाटक और महाराष्ट्र के कई समुदाय करते हैं। नीचे 2035 के तेलुगु त्योहार और व्रत की तारीखें हैं।

The Telugu panchangam (తెలుగు పంచాంగం) follows the Amanta lunisolar calendar, where each month runs from one new moon to the next. It is used across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana and by many Kannada and Marathi communities. The dates below are the festivals and vrats of 2035 in Telugu naming, worked out for Delhi (IST).

Telugu New Year (Ugadi) / ఉగాది

The Telugu year begins on Chaitra Shukla Padyami, which is Ugadi. In 2035 it falls on 9 April. Ugadi is welcomed with Ugadi pachadi, a mix of six tastes for the six moods of the year, and with the reading of the new year's panchangam.

Popular Telugu festivals and vrats

  • Ugadi: the Telugu New Year in March or April.
  • Varalakshmi Vratam: observed by married women on the Friday before Shravana Purnima.
  • Nagula Chavithi: Karthika Shukla Chaturthi, when snake deities are worshipped.
  • Atla Tadde: a Gauri vrat kept on Ashvayuja Krishna Tadiya (third tithi).
  • Sankashtahara Chaturthi: the monthly Ganesha fast after Purnima, named differently in each month.
  • Ekadashi and Pradosh: the fortnightly Vishnu and Shiva vrats.

For other regional and national dates, see the Hindu Calendar and Indian Holidays. For Telugu daily timings, use Gowri Panchangam and Rahu Kalam.

Telugu Festivals FAQs

Which calendar does the Telugu panchangam follow?

The Amanta lunisolar calendar, in which each month runs from one new moon to the next and has Shukla and Krishna pakshas.

When is Ugadi in 2035?

Ugadi, the Telugu New Year, falls on 9 April 2035.

When is Varalakshmi Vratam in 2035?

Varalakshmi Vratam is on Friday, 17 August 2035, the Friday before Shravana Purnima.

Why do Telugu festival dates differ from the North Indian calendar?

The Telugu calendar names vrats differently (for example Sankashtahara for Sankashti), and a tithi that spans two days can put a festival one day apart in different traditions.

Dates are for Delhi (IST) and may differ by a day in other cities or traditions. Confirm important festivals with your family pandit.
